Given that $f(x)=|x-2|+1,$ on which of the following intervals is $f(x)$ invertible?

- $x\in (-\infty ,1]$
- $x\in (1,\infty )$
- $x\in (2,4]$
feedback.worked_solution:
The graph of the function $f(x)=|x-2|+1$ can be obtained in the following way:

- Take the curve $y=|x|.$

- Translate it by $2$ units to the right,  to get $y=|x-2|.$

- Finally, translate $y=|x-2|$ by $1$ unit up to get $f(x)=|x-2|+1.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14068486/assets/ceab1637313ae53869cc1e59f6a56ad6cb920a83dffba482558b696188df0d36.png)

A function is invertible on a particular interval if and only if it's a one-to-one function on that interval. To determine the intervals on which the function is invertible, we use the horizontal line test. 

- The function $f(x)$ is invertible on each of the intervals $x\in (-\infty ,1]$ and $x\in (2,4].$ On these intervals, a horizontal line will intersect the curve at most once, no matter where we draw the line.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14068486/assets/a47169838785b6f4ac78253252bcedc3c2cb752a655feac9945e20dd40563b4f.png)

  

- The function $f(x)$ is not invertible on the interval $x\in (1,\infty ).$ On this interval, some horizontal lines will intersect the curve more than once.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14068486/assets/14ed35294e1179ffd9efaf87fa8ac1eb99853a7da344e462c2cb0dda74c3b78f.png)

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only".
